root.name: Philidor Defense: Lion Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 Nf6 4. Nc3 Nbd7

overview: Black builds the Philidor set-up with ...Nbd7, ...Be7, ...O-O and ...c6, keeping the e5 pawn and the d6 pawn in a compact chain. White has more space and can choose 5.Bc4 with quick castling, aiming at f7, or exchange on e5, and play for central pressure. The game is a slow manoeuvring fight where Black waits for a ...exd4 or ...d5 break.

white_ideas.idea: Develop with Bc4, O-O, Re1, a4 and keep the centre tension, aiming at Ng5 or d5.
Exchange on e5 to reach open lines and use the space edge.

black_ideas.idea: Hold e5 with ...c6, ...Be7 and ...O-O, then break with ...exd4 or ...d5.
Keep a compact position and use the Lion set-up's flexibility with ...Qc7.

typical_structures.structure: Black pawns on e5/d6 with c6 support, White with e4/d4 and more space.

character.notes: Compact Black set-up, few quick tactics, hard to break down; Black may be slightly passive.

soundness.notes: A recognised Philidor set-up; sound though slightly passive.

structure.notes: d4/e5 tension is held or resolved later; undecided centre.

approach.notes: A recognised Philidor line, played at all levels, less common than e5 main lines.

level.notes: Needs understanding of when to break; moderate memory.

sublines_that_differ.name: 6.dxe5 dxe5
sublines_that_differ.how: Opens the position and leads to tactics around f7.

approach.reason: Less common but played by strong players; not offbeat.

level.reason: Plans matter more than long theory.

plans.reason: White's central space against Black's compact set-up.
